trickyParts: Why rewrite at send time: the machine owns the pending delivery; a rewrite inside admission's transaction would be overwritten by the machine's next write of its memory. The record already says which tree owes a decision, so no new durable state is needed, and any route an issue leaves a tree by is covered. The narrowed task is persisted before the send, so a restore reads the same text; the delivery id is kept.
A mark whose issue the record does not hold is kept, never dropped: a decision is dropped from a task only where the record shows another tree owes it.

propertyModelGaps: Spec decisions through the outbox's parkDecision, RelayNotParked and a session's decision: every keep path calls record.RelayParkedDecision, which writes one parked_decisions row keyed (issue, ref) and nothing else the naming or telling reads; RelayNotParked and a session's decision keep nothing, so the entry path cannot change how many times a row is told.

readmitted_approvals: keyed by the issue whose spec it is, with the same claim and hold columns, and every claim, hold, tell and release statement acts on both tables keyed by the same outbox row or delivery, so the pair moves through the states exactly when a decision of the same row does.

Retired claims: retire clears the delivery's holds in its transaction (releaseKeptDecisions at RetireDelivery), so a retired claim's rows return to KEPT for the tree their issue stands in; the model reaches retire through RetireDelivery at every turn end and suspension.
Issue deletion: the daemon has no code path that deletes an issue record; parked_decisions.issue cascades if a person deletes one by hand, and then no architect of that issue exists to tell.

An unroutable notice and a re-hold whose budget is spent finish the row without telling, so its deletion releases its claims (on delete set null) and the architect's next ready names them, the same ending as 'refused', which is modelled.

Concurrency and time: naming claims only rows with no counting claim or hold in its own transaction; settlements and hand-overs take the facts' advisory lock; the model runs due rows on concurrent goroutines and in random order and drops finishes, which covers what backoff, lease expiry or a re-hold delay can order.

oracle: A catch-up names the generation current when the daemon decided to send it (read at the start of its publish). The publish is network I/O outside every transaction; a re-admission landing inside it is followed by the new generation's own catch-up, queued behind it (earlierNoticeFor). The architect agreed (A).

A refused or denied catch-up keeps its decisions unclaimed; quiesce ends a refusal as it ends in real life, by relaunching the architect, whose ready names them. The architect agreed to keep that ending (B), on condition that a decision never vanishes silently: lingerExpired logs each decision still owed.

A decision counts as told when told once to the architect of the tree its issue stood in at that telling. After a child's hand-over, what was still kept or held is owed to the child's architect; one extra telling to the old tree, by a row composed before the hand-over, is allowed.

A decision is owed to the architect of the tree its issue stands in, moving with the issue whenever it moves while still kept or held; a telling to the tree it left counts at most once, by a row composed before it left.
